object.description: How the wave function Ψ of a quantum system changes in time: the Hamiltonian, the system's energy, drives it, with Planck's constant setting the scale. Schrödinger, a professor at the University of Zürich, published wave mechanics in four papers in 1926; the time-dependent form shown here is in the fourth, received on 21 June. It is the equation of chemistry: the periodic table, the shapes of molecules and the behaviour of the electrons in the chips further along this lane all come out of it.
facts: Schrödinger conceived the equation over Christmas 1925 at a villa in Arosa; the first paper reached the Annalen der Physik on 27 January 1926.
Max Born showed the same year that |Ψ|² is a probability, the reading Schrödinger himself never liked.
Schrödinger shared the 1933 Nobel Prize in Physics with Paul Dirac; his cat, the thought experiment, came in 1935.
